title: The Kirkpatrick Model
supports: Four levels (Reaction, Learning, Behavior, Results) and what each measures; relevance as the key part of Level 1; confidence and commitment at Level 2 as early signs of use on the job; start planning at Level 4 with leading and lagging indicators; do not wait 90 days to measure Level 3; model described as cyclical; additions: performance environment, return on expectations, return on performance, contributive ROI; history: Donald Kirkpatrick 1950s, Jim and Wendy Kayser Kirkpatrick 2010s, 2026 update by Vanessa Milara Alzate. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Don Kirkpatrick
supports: Donald Kirkpatrick set out the four levels in the 1950s, around his PhD dissertation on a human relations training programme for supervisors; Professor Emeritus at the University of Wisconsin; died May 2014. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Stories of Impact
supports: Vendor-reported results: Maryland Transit Administration accident reduction programme cut bus accident claims by 46% over five years; Indiana University Health EMR rollout raised on-the-job compliance scores by over 20% and cut medication errors of severity E or higher by 67% over three years; IRS new hire training costs cut by 50%. Methods not published on the page. Opened with WebFetch.

title: ROI Methodology
supports: Five levels (reaction and planned action, learning, application and implementation, business impact, ROI); isolating the effects of the programme (control groups, trend lines, estimates); converting data to money; fully loaded costs; BCR = benefits / costs; ROI % = net benefits / costs; intangible benefits; conservative standards. Jack and Patti Phillips lead the Institute. Opened with WebFetch.

title: LTEM: The Learning-Transfer Evaluation Model
supports: Eight tiers; lower tiers cannot validate learning success, upper half measures transfer; presented as an improvement on the four-level model, which it says put all learning in one bucket; separates knowledge, decision-making and task performance; Version 13 released 31 October 2024. Opened with WebFetch.

title: The Science of Training and Development in Organizations: What Matters in Practice (Salas, Tannenbaum, Kraiger and Smith-Jentsch, Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 2012)
supports: Before training: a supportive learning climate and a training needs analysis (what to train, who, how it fits the system); during: the right mindset and sound instructional principles; after: transfer to the job and evaluation. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Learning at work 2023
supports: Published 27 June 2023; YouGov online survey January to February 2023 of 1,108 people responsible for learning at work, 91% UK-based; 29% name the skills gap as top priority; 53% say L&D workload increased; 57% now seek to understand a performance issue before recommending a solution, up from 32% in 2021. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Evaluating learning and development (factsheet)
supports: Evaluation should be linked to identified performance gaps and learning aligned with business objectives; page dated 18 August 2025; most of the factsheet is member-only, only the open part was read. Opened with WebFetch.

title: 2025 Workplace Learning Report: The rise of career champions
supports: Survey of 937 L&D and HR professionals and 679 learners plus LinkedIn platform data to September 2024; 49% say executives worry staff lack skills to execute strategy; 71% of L&D pros exploring, experimenting with or using AI in their work; 15% of employees say their manager helped them build a career plan in the past six months; 36% of organisations are 'career development champions'. Opened with WebFetch.

title: 2025 Training Industry Report
supports: US training spend $102.8 billion in 2025, up 4.9%; $874 per learner (from $774); 40 hours of training per employee (from 47); share of training hours by method (online 34%, classroom 28%, virtual classroom 24%, blended 22%); US organisations with 100 or more employees; survey April to July 2025. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Onboarding New Employees: Maximizing Success (Talya N. Bauer, SHRM Foundation, 2010)
publisher: SHRM Foundation (copy hosted by University of Georgia Student Affairs)
supports: Four Cs (compliance, clarification, culture, connection); passive (about 30% of firms), high potential (about 50%) and proactive onboarding; levers: self-efficacy, role clarity, social integration, knowledge of culture; IBM's Assimilation Process (affirming, beginning in the first 30 days, connecting through the first year with a coach check-in at two months); Corning Glass Works structured orientation finding. PDF saved by WebFetch and converted to text.

title: 1-2-4-All
publisher: Liberating Structures (Henri Lipmanowicz and Keith McCandless)
supports: Steps and timings: invitation, 1 minute alone, 2 minutes in pairs, 5 minutes in fours, about 7 minutes whole group; purpose is to include every voice; 1-3-All variant for online or large groups; content licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Opened with WebFetch.

title: SFIA 9
supports: SFIA 9 published October 2024; seven levels of responsibility; 26 skills added; documents freely available after registration. Opened with WebFetch.

title: SFIA 9 levels of responsibility
supports: Level names: 1 Follow, 2 Assist, 3 Apply, 4 Enable, 5 Ensure, advise, 6 Initiate, influence, 7 Set strategy, inspire, mobilise; levels defined by generic attributes. Opened with WebFetch.

title: What is ESCO
supports: ESCO v1.2.1 (updated 10 December 2025): 3,039 occupations and 13,939 skills in 28 languages; free portal, download and API; used to match jobseekers to jobs and suggest training. Opened with WebFetch.

title: O*NET OnLine
publisher: US Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration (National Center for O*NET Development)
supports: Free occupation data for 900+ occupations: over 19,000 task statements, skills, knowledge, work activities, tools and technology; site updated 6 October 2026. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Employing an apprentice
supports: England: apprenticeships last 8 months to 6 years; employer makes an apprenticeship agreement and training plan, pays at least the minimum wage, gives time off in the working week for training and has the apprentice work with experienced staff; links to funding and provider search. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Apprenticeships search (standards, foundation apprenticeships and units)
supports: 2,087 apprenticeships listed as of 6 November 2026; programme types: apprenticeship standards, foundation apprenticeships and apprenticeship units; 15 technical routes; minimum duration 8 months for starts from 1 August 2025 (12 months before); English and maths exit requirements optional for apprentices aged 19+ from 11 February 2025. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Apprenticeship funding rules: 2026 to 2027
supports: Rules for England apply to apprenticeships starting 1 August 2026 to 31 July 2027; version 3, last updated 3 August 2026; each apprentice is funded under the rules for their start date. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Registered Apprenticeship Program
supports: Components: paid job with rising wages, structured on-the-job learning with a mentor, supplemental classroom education, a nationally recognised credential; programmes approved and validated by the US Department of Labor or a State Apprenticeship Agency. Opened with WebFetch.

title: AI Literacy - Questions & Answers
supports: AI Act Article 4 applies to providers and deployers since 2 February 2025; supervision and enforcement by national authorities from 2 August 2026; no certificate required, internal records suggested; no fixed format; suggested minimum content; the Digital Omnibus on AI (mid-July 2026) kept the duty but removed a mandated 'sufficient' level; page updated 20 October 2026. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Health and safety training (HSE guidance for employers)
supports: Great Britain: employers must give clear instructions and information and adequate training and supervision; particular needs of new recruits, people changing jobs or taking on extra duties, young employees and safety representatives; page updated 6 June 2025. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Training Requirements in OSHA Standards (OSHA 2254-09R 2015)
publisher: US Occupational Safety and Health Administration
supports: Many OSHA standards contain explicit training requirements; required training must be provided by and paid for by employers; keeping a record of all safety training is advised; some standards require training in a manner the employee understands. PDF saved by WebFetch and converted to text.

title: The OSH Framework Directive (Directive 89/391/EEC)
publisher: European Agency for Safety and Health at Work (EU-OSHA)
supports: EU framework directive of 12 June 1989: employers must ensure each worker receives adequate safety and health training; costs of safety measures may not be passed to workers. Opened with WebFetch.

title: The 70:20:10 Model
supports: The institute that promotes the model calls 70:20:10 a reference model and a practical metaphor, not a fixed rule; the ratio varies with the work and results needed; structured learning still matters. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Replication and Analysis of Ebbinghaus' Forgetting Curve (Murre and Dros, PLOS ONE, 2015)
supports: A one-person replication (the second author) using lists of nonsense syllables and the savings method; curve resembles Ebbinghaus's 1880 result; shows how narrow the original evidence is for workplace 'forgetting curve' percentages. Opened with WebFetch.

title: Job Instruction
supports: Training Within Industry Job Instruction, created during the Second World War to train people new to their tasks: break a job into the one best way (what, how and why), present and demonstrate, let workers learn by doing, check progress with coaching and questions. Opened with WebFetch.

title: L&D tools: Building your business case - a practical pathway
supports: CIPD tool in three stages for an evidence-led business case for learning, built for real organisations including small ones, where cases often succeed through conversations as well as documents; published 12 August 2026; detail is member-only. Opened with WebFetch.
